searchText: the 1024 stack items also include pointers to reference memory right? (each of which would take up 2 slots) The stack has always been 1024 items of 256 bits. 1 item is more than enough to index a location in memory, if that is your question <@!726055386142212216>. Have a look at https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3670 which is the simplest first step towards that. Thanks, <@!425279588009246720>, I hadn't considered that way of going wrong. As other instructions with immediate data get added the same problem will arise. Could these be considered a form of invalid instruction? I'm stressing the concept of safety here because it arises often with no agreed definition. I think I can validate the properties I give with fewer restrictions than EIP-615, and without deprecating dynamic jumps - just taming them. That is because I think that in actual code the destinations of most dynamic jumps can be limited to a finite set by a simple static analysis. But the proposal remains a Draft until I'm sure. https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3779 And even minimal taming of dynamic jumps would let static versions of subroutines and jumps can ensure safety. https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2315

excerpts.content:
I'm stressing the concept of safety here because it arises often with no agreed definition.

I think I can validate the properties I give with fewer restrictions than EIP-615, and without deprecating dynamic jumps - just taming them.

That is because I think that in actual code the destinations of most dynamic jumps can be limited to a finite set by a simple static analysis. But the proposal remains a Draft until I'm sure.
https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3779

And even minimal taming of dynamic jumps would let static versions of subroutines and jumps can ensure safety.
https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2315
